summary: This guide covers APHIS new-hire onboarding from candidate selection through pre-employment clearance (TSN, ISA test, fingerprints, HRO 1197, suitability), the final offer and EOD date, arrival preparation, first-week orientation, eAuthentication and Linc Pass activation, and check-ins at 14 to 30 and 30 to 90 days. The supervisor (also called the Hiring Official or Hiring Manager) runs most steps, working with the new hire, MRPBS HRD and its Personnel Security Section, ITD, Program Administrative Staff, AAMD, FATA, and other support offices.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The fingerprint check or suitability determination comes back unfavorable. Nobody is told what to do next, so the supervisor keeps ordering equipment and messaging a candidate whose offer may not proceed.
risks.cause: Appendix 1 makes a favorable SAC and suitability determination a condition for the EOD, but no section states who tells the supervisor or the candidate, or what happens next (D5 'No' branch is UNDEFINED).
risks.impact: Wasted arrival preparation, confused communication with the candidate, and possible mishandling of a sensitive personnel outcome.

quantified_impact.metric: Decision branches with no next step
quantified_impact.basis: Decision D5 in the current state map

risks.severity_reason: An unfavorable result is uncommon, but when it happens it touches a sensitive personnel decision with no guidance.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: One of the five prerequisites (TSN, ISA, onboarding documents, SAC, suitability) stays open. HRD does not set an EOD, and nobody is assigned to find and chase the missing item, so the start date quietly slips.
risks.cause: Appendix 1 says HRD sets the EOD 'ONLY AFTER' all prerequisites are met, but names no owner or escalation path for an unmet prerequisite (D7 'No' branch is UNDEFINED).
risks.impact: The start date is delayed, the candidate is left waiting, and the candidate may withdraw.

quantified_impact.metric: Prerequisites that each block the EOD
quantified_impact.basis: Appendix 1: TSN accepted, ISA finished, onboarding documents received, SAC completed, favorable suitability

risks.severity_reason: Any one of five items can stall the EOD, and none has a follow-up owner, so this is likely and it directly delays the start.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The fingerprints and HRO 1197 are shipped by courier and sit untracked until HRD happens to receive them. A late or lost package goes unnoticed while the EOD cannot be set.
risks.cause: The 'When Legal Selection is Confirmed' checklist requires a UPS/FedEx tracking number but gives no receipt confirmation or follow-up step. Appendix 1 says the EOD will not be set until the fingerprints and HRO 1197 arrive.
risks.impact: The whole clearance timeline slides. The example timeline shows HR waiting about two weeks for fingerprints.
risks.severity_reason: The SOP's own example shows this is the longest wait, and the EOD depends on it.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The supervisor tells the candidate a start date at selection, but HRD sets a different date after clearance. Arrival preparation is then timed to the wrong day.
risks.cause: The SOP gives three versions of who sets the EOD and when. Flowchart - Before Hire has the Hiring Manager establish the EOD with HR Staffing at selection. Appendix 1 says HRD sets it only after the prerequisites are met. 'When the Final Offer has been Accepted' has the supervisor coordinate with HR to establish it after the final offer, which already contains the EOD.
risks.impact: The candidate gets conflicting information, and equipment, badge, and sponsor arrangements may be ready on the wrong date.

quantified_impact.metric: Sections giving a different EOD owner or timing
quantified_impact.basis: Flowchart - Before Hire; Appendix 1; When the Final Offer has been Accepted

risks.severity_reason: The conflict is likely to cause confusion on every hire, but the impact is rework rather than loss.

risks.cause: Appendix 1 and Flowchart - Before Hire say to submit the Service Now request as soon as the name appears in the GAL (before hire). The First Day - First Week checklist lists the same SNOW request as a first-week task.
risks.impact: The new hire loses productive time, and part of the 30-day username/password window may be spent waiting.

quantified_impact.basis: Appendix 1 item 4; First Day - First Week checklist

risks.severity_reason: Supervisors are likely to follow the checklist they work from, which delays access for the new hire.

risks.severity_reason: Detection is built in late against a hard 30-day access deadline.

risks.what_could_go_wrong: The supervisor emails the wrong ATAC address about a missing eAuth invitation, and the request is delayed or never handled.

risks.impact: The access problem takes longer to resolve.
risks.severity_reason: One address may forward to the other, but the conflict adds avoidable delay.

risks.cause: The 14 to 30 Days checklist sends each request to a different office (AAMD twice, FATA, FMD Travel Team, International Services) with no tracking. 'When the Final Offer has been Accepted' says contact with POCs is ongoing until the new hire is fully functioning.

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.proposed_change: The paper Supervisor/Manager Checklist becomes an Onboarding Tracker: a Power Apps form over a SharePoint list, with one record per new hire. It holds milestone fields (TSN accepted or declined, ISA, fingerprints shipped and received, SAC/suitability, additional clearances, EOD, items collected outside the system and their owners). HRD and the supervisor update one shared record.
recommendations.reason: Status currently lives in separate checklists and email, so prerequisites, additional clearances, and the EOD have no single owner or source.
implementation_steps: Create a SharePoint list 'Onboarding Tracker' with columns for the new hire, supervisor, HRD POC, location, Linc Pass exempt (Y/N), each Appendix 1 prerequisite, additional clearances (S23), transcript and drug test collection owner, and EOD (editable only by HRD).
Build a Power Apps canvas app from the list, with views for supervisor, HRD, and Administrative Staff.
Set item-level permissions so HRD owns the EOD and prerequisite fields.
Add a status choice that includes 'TSN declined - closed'.
Pilot with one Program and adjust the fields.

impact.basis: Estimate of supervisor time saved chasing status by email; the map shows no step removed by this change alone.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: Manual calendar reminders are replaced by a flow that runs when HRD enters the EOD in the tracker. It creates dated Planner tasks and Outlook reminders for every checklist phase (first week, 14 to 30 days, 30 to 90 days), including the day 30 and day 45 benefits check-ins and the I-9 deadline.
recommendations.reason: Every checklist item is time-boxed relative to the EOD and is rule-based.
implementation_steps: Create a SharePoint list 'Checklist Template' with each checklist item, its phase, its offset in days from the EOD, and its owner role.
Build a flow triggered when the EOD in the Onboarding Tracker is modified.
For each template item, calculate the due date (EOD plus offset) and create a Planner task assigned to the supervisor or Administrative Staff.
Create Outlook events for the day 30 and day 45 benefits check-ins.
Add a daily recurrence flow that emails a digest of overdue tasks to their owners.

impact.basis: Estimate of time to set reminders for about 50 checklist items by hand; this is an estimate.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: The Hiring Manager logs the courier tracking number in the tracker, which asks HRD Personnel Security to confirm receipt. If receipt is not confirmed within a configurable number of days, the flow reminds both parties.
recommendations.reason: The shipment is the longest wait in the example timeline and has no follow-up.
implementation_steps: Add 'Tracking number', 'Shipped date', and 'Received by PSS' columns to the tracker.
Build a flow triggered when the tracking number is entered that emails HRD Personnel Security a receipt-confirmation link.
Add a scheduled check: if not received within the threshold the Program sets, email the Hiring Manager and HRD PSS.
Update the prerequisite status when receipt is confirmed.

impact.basis: Estimate; makes the S20 handoff visible but does not remove it. Wait reduction is not claimed.

recommendations.proposed_change: Based on the location in the tracker, a flow emails the new hire either the Live Scan locations list and operator contact or SF-87 card instructions, along with the HRO 1197 requirement.
recommendations.reason: The Typical Hiring Timeframe note says helping with fingerprinting 'can speed up the Onboarding process significantly', and the routing at D3 is rule-based.
implementation_steps: Add a 'Near Live Scan site' choice column (DC/MD, Minneapolis, Ames, Fort Collins, Raleigh, None).
Build a flow triggered when TSN accepted is set.
Use a condition to send an email template with the Live Scan list link or SF-87 instructions.
Create a Planner task for the supervisor to mail the cards if the new hire is not near a Live Scan site.

impact.basis: Estimate of time to look up the location and write instructions.

recommendations.reason: Standard content is retyped for every hire.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: A daily flow checks whether the new hire's name appears in the directory and notifies the Hiring Manager right away, with a prefilled Service Now network/PIV-exclusion request. This sets the pre-hire timing as the standard.
recommendations.reason: The GAL trigger is currently watched by hand, and two sections give conflicting timing.
implementation_steps: Add a 'Listed in GAL' column to the tracker.
Build a scheduled flow using Office 365 Users 'Search for users' on the new hire's name for open records.
When found, update the tracker and send the Hiring Manager a Teams or email notice with the SNOW link and field values.
Optionally use the ServiceNow connector (premium) to create the request directly after the Hiring Manager confirms.
Ask the SOP owner to remove the SNOW item from the First Day - First Week checklist.
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Automate + Office 365 Users + ServiceNow connector

impact.basis: Estimate; removes repeated manual GAL checks. The handoff from ITD to Hiring Manager remains but is now notified.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: At EOD plus 5 days, a flow asks the new hire directly (Teams adaptive card, or email to a personal address) whether both the eAuth and Linc Pass invitations arrived. It records the answer in the tracker, sends junk-folder instructions if one is missing, and alerts the supervisor if it is still missing.
recommendations.reason: Invitations arrive 1-5 days after onboarding, but confirmation is scheduled at day 14 or later, against a 30-day grace period.
implementation_steps: Add 'eAuth invite received' and 'Linc Pass invite received' columns to the tracker.
Build a daily flow that selects records where EOD plus 5 equals today and Linc Pass exempt is No.
Post an adaptive card to the new hire and wait for the response.
If an invite is missing, send the Appendix 2 junk and deleted folder instructions and re-ask after one business day.
If still missing, update the tracker and notify the supervisor, which starts the escalation flow (A8).
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Automate + Teams adaptive cards + SharePoint

impact.basis: Removes the Supervisor-to-New Hire and New Hire-to-Supervisor handoffs after S64 and S65. Moves the check from day 14 (earliest in the 14 to 30 Days checklist) to day 5 (latest invitation arrival in Appendix 1), which is 9 days. Minutes are an estimate.

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.proposed_change: When the tracker shows an invitation is still missing, a flow sends a standardized escalation email to the single confirmed ATAC address or to HRD PSS, logs the date, and reminds the supervisor if there is no resolution before a set point in the 30-day grace period.

Build a flow triggered when an 'invite missing' status is set.

Schedule a follow-up reminder to the supervisor based on the days remaining in the 30-day grace period.

Record the I-9 return date in the tracker.
